title: High-Performance Dual-Channel PCF-SPR  Biosensor for Broad-Range Multi-Analyte  Biomedical Sensing
summary:
This paper proposes a dual-core, dual-channel 
Photonic crystal fiber-based surface plasmon resonance (PCF
SPR) biosensor, numerically evaluated via the finite element 
method (FEM), and capable of simultaneous multi-analyte 
detection over a refractive index (RI) range of 1.18-1.42 using 
gold as the plasmonic layer. The proposed design has maximum 
wavelength sensitivity of 38000nm/RIU, amplitude sensitivity of 
1414.43 RIU−1, figure of merit of 655.17 RIU−1 and sensor 
resolution of 9×10−6 RIU. There exists no crosstalk between the 
two channels and the structural tolerance analysis shows that 
the design is robust under reasonable fabrication deviations. In 
addition to RI sensing, the sensor is able to discriminate six 
cancer cell types, with a maximum sensitivity of 7142.85 nm/RIU 
for MCF-7 cells, and four bacterial pathogens, measuring up to 
4878.04 nm/RIU for Enterococcus faecalis. These findings 
highlight its potential for practical diagnostic applications.

title: Physical Layer Security Analysis of RIS-Assisted Multicasting with MVDR Beamforming Over κ-µ Shadowed Fading Channels
summary:
This paper presents a physical layer security analysis of RIS-assisted multicasting with minimum variance dis
tortionless response (MVDR) beamforming over κ-µ shadowed fading channels. The MVDR framework is applied at the RIS to jointly maximize the received SINR at the weakest legitimate destination user and suppress the signal leakage toward a passive eavesdropper. By treating the cascade RIS channel as a virtual array, the MVDR weight vector is derived in closed form via the Sherman–Morrison identity, and the resulting SINR is shown to follow a κ-µ shadowed distribution through moment-matching.
Leveraging this statistical characterization, closed-form expres
sions are derived for three security metrics applicable to K
user multicast scenarios: the ergodic secrecy capacity (ESC), the
probability of non-zero secrecy capacity (PNZSC), and the secure
outage probability (SOP). Monte Carlo simulations validate the
analytical results, and numerical evaluations demonstrate that
increasing the number of RIS elements N, the Rician factor κ,
and the multipath clustering parameter µ consistently improves
secrecy performance. Results further confirm that MVDR beam
forming provides a measurable security gain over conventional
coherent phase alignment, particularly when the eavesdropper
channel is strong.

title: Secure Outage Performance Analysis of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface-Aided Networks with Selection Combining Diversity Scheme
summary: This paper investigates the outage-based secrecy performance of reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted wireless communication systems with selection combining (SC) diversity over Rayleigh fading channels in the presence of a passive multi-antenna eavesdropper. Unlike existing RIS-assisted secrecy studies that mainly focus on single-antenna reception without diversity combining, this work considers a single-antenna source communicating with a multi-antenna destination through an RIS, while a passive multi-antenna eavesdropper attempts to intercept the transmission. Since the direct links between the source and both the destination and the eavesdropper are blocked by physical obstacles, all communications are established through an RIS equipped with N passive reflecting elements. Exact closed-form analytical expressions for the probability of non-zero secrecy capacity (PNZSC), intercept probability (IP), and secure outage probability (SOP) are derived and verified through Monte Carlo simulations. Numerical results demonstrate that increasing the number of RIS reflecting elements N and legitimate receiver antennas Nd significantly improves secrecy performance, whereas increasing the number of eavesdropper antennas Ne degrades secrecy reliability. Furthermore, RIS deployment can partially compensate for stronger eavesdropping conditions without increasing transmit-side complexity. The obtained results confirm that integrating RIS technology with low-complexity SC diversity provides an effective and energy-efficient solution for enhancing physical-layer security in future wireless networks.

title: Highly Sensitive N-FK51A/Cu/ZnSe/BP-Based SPR Biosensor for Dengue Virus Detection: A TMM and FEM Approach
summary: This work demonstrates the design and optimization of a multilayer prism-based Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) biosensor intended for the early and accurate detection of blood cells infected with the dengue virus. Our proposed structure utilizes an N-FK51A prism that is coated with copper (Cu), zinc selenide (ZnSe), and a monolayer of black phosphorus (BP). This configuration creates an optimized plasmonic interface that improves light-matter interaction. To determine the optimal thickness of each layer, we applied Finite Element Method (FEM) simulation in COMSOL Multiphysics and Transfer Matrix Method (TMM) analysis in MATLAB. The biosensor shows a peak angular sensitivity of 327.71°/RIU, full width at half maximum (FWHM) of 1.89 deg., 0.7874 deg-1 detection accuracy (DA), and a quality factor (QF) of 156.68 RIU-1 for dengue-affected hemoglobin cells. Close agreement of results obtained from FEM and TMM confirms the computational approaches accuracy and the reliability of the proposed model. Overall, the proposed N-FK51A/Cu/ZnSe/BP biosensor offers a cost-effective and promising platform for rapid detection dengue virus.

title: Design and optimization of a CaF₂/Cu/GO/InN multilayer SPR biosensor for label-free and highly sensitive tuberculosis diagnosis
summary: This study focuses on the design and optimization of a novel, high-performance prism-based Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) biosensor for the early detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis. The designed multilayer structure has five layers, which are CaF2 prism, Cu as a plasmonic layer, GO as a bio-functional layer, an InN as a high-index dielectric layer, and a sensing medium as the top layer. To optimize the materials and their respective thicknesses, the Transfer Matrix Method (TMM) in MATLAB has been utilized, and validation of the results is carried out using Finite Element Method (FEM) simulations in COMSOL Multiphysics. The results obtained from both TMM and FEM are similar. The optimized configuration, with layer thicknesses of 40 nm for Cu,10 nm for GO, and 5 nm for InN, achieves a maximum angular sensitivity of 588.33∘/ RIU and a quality factor (QF) of 156.68 RIU −1 between 1.351 and 1.348 for the refractive index, which surpasses all previously reported TB-specific SPR sensors. Additionally, the sensor exhibits a low full-width at half maximum (FWHM) of 3.75° and a detection accuracy (DA) of 0.3067deg−1. A study of thickness variations in Cu, GO, and InN through parametric analysis confirmed improved plasmon coupling, improved detection accuracy, and higher quality factors. This biosensor offers a promising platform for rapid, label-free, and highly sensitive tuberculosis diagnosis, as it integrates low optical dispersion from CaF2, strong plasmonic resonance from Cu, effective biomolecular adsorption from GO, and excellent light confinement from InN.
